Hi Elena,

Thanks for the follow-up. I promised more concrete artifacts — attaching a Processing Map (redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf) and a short KMS integration note. Key points below in case you need to paste into your questionnaire: 

1) Regions and runtime locality
- Hosted API: Customers choose region at the API key level. For US customers we host inference in: us-east-1 (primary), us-west-2 (secondary).
- Requests routed to the nearest healthy endpoint. Transit between regions is limited to failover and does not perform cross-border analytics.

2) Subprocessors (roles)
- Cloud compute: AWS (EC2/GPU instances) and GCP (TPU/VMs for specific customers).
- Observability: DataPulse (aggregated metrics only; traces are sampled and PII is redacted).
- Logging & storage: S3-compatible object stores managed within the chosen region; backups replicate only within the region by default unless customer enables cross-region DR.

3) Data use and training
- We do NOT use customer request payloads or user-provided content to train models unless explicitly contracted and opt-in is documented. Audit trail exists for any opt-in.

4) Retention and deletion
- Default retention: 30 days for request payloads (configurable down to 0 days for Dedicated/Private customers).
- Logs/metrics: 90 days by default for debugging; can be adjusted via plan or enterprise contract.
- Deletion APIs & Console: immediate soft-delete is available; hard deletion (wipe) process runs within 48–72 hours with audit proof.

5) Cross-border specifics
- For EU data residency requirements we offer region pinning (eu-west-1) and Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) where no data leaves the EU.
- For Atlas (US-only customer), we will keep processing within US regions unless you explicitly request multi-region DR.

Attachments: redwood_processing_map_v2.pdf (map of processing paths), kms_integration_notes.txt (how we integrate customer KMS/HSM).

Happy to schedule a 30-min call to walk this through.

Elena — quick technical confirmations: 

1) BYOK / KMS: When a customer uses customer-managed keys (BYOK), encryption/decryption for request payloads occurs within the region and within FIPS-validated KMS endpoints when required. Plaintext is never written to external telemetry systems. Any temporary cache used for inference is memory-resident on the GPU host and is not persisted to cross-region storage. We document the key wrapping and audit flow in kms_integration_notes.txt attached.

2) Monitoring traces: DataPulse receives only aggregated metrics and sampled traces with PII redaction. We have an agreement that DataPulse processes telemetry only within US zones for US customers; no sampled payload snippets are sent outside the US. Traces containing sensitive fields are redacted before export.

Additional notes:
- Backups and DR replication are opt-in for cross-region.
- If Atlas needs an EU-only contract clause, we support Private/VPC deployments and on-prem packs.

If you'd like, we can provide a narrow statement of fact for your security binder (signed by our SOC2 owner).

— Karthik
